title: Difficulties in Learning the Synergetic Nature of English Aspectual Forms and Evolution of Pedagogy
text_snippet: Difficulties in Learning the Synergetic Nature of English Aspectual Forms and Evolution of Pedagogy English aspectual forms remain a significant challenge for EFL learners because their accurate use depends on the interaction of grammar, semantics, discourse context, and communicative purpose. In Uzbekistan, where English is primarily learned through formal classroom instruction and learners have limited exposure to authentic language use, mastering aspectual distinctions remains particularly difficult. This study investigates the challenges associated with learning the synergetic nature of English aspectual forms and evaluates the effectiveness of an innovative pedagogical approach designed to improve learners’ conceptual understanding and communicative use. The study is significant because it provides evidence-based insights that can inform grammar instruction, curriculum development, and teacher education in Uzbek EFL classrooms. A mixed-methods research design was employed. Quantitative data were collected from 60 undergraduate EFL teachers, who were assigned to experimental and control groups and completed pre- and post-tests measuring their understanding and use of English aspectual forms. title: Investigating Morphosyntactic Patterns and Metaphorical Interpretation of Compound Words in Walt Whitman’s Song of Myself: A Construction Morphology Approach
text_snippet: Investigating Morphosyntactic Patterns and Metaphorical Interpretation of Compound Words in Walt Whitman’s Song of Myself: A Construction Morphology Approach As a word formation process, compounding is essential to poetry because it enriches the poetic language, making it more compressed, concise, metaphorically dense, and effective. The article aims to investigate the morphosyntactic and metaphorical aspects of the compound words employed by the American poet Walt Whitman in his renowned poem Song of Myself. Whitman’s way of compounding words is a distinctive stylistic feature that sets his poetry apart from the work of other American poets. He created compound words that are unconventional and innovative. A Constructional Morphology (CM) approach has been employed to analyze the data. The Blending Theory of Metaphor (BTM) was also highly utilized in interpreting any metaphor encoded in the compound words. The data were solely collected from Song of Myself. A total of 627 compounds were identified and statistically analyzed, while 10 compounds were randomly selected and qualitatively analyzed. Whitman’s creation of compound words is driven by his intention to shed light on certain unique themes that are closely connected to his beliefs, visions, poetic identity, and outlook. title: Redefining Literature Reviews: A Scoping Review of AI-Powered Research Assistants
text_snippet: Redefining Literature Reviews: A Scoping Review of AI-Powered Research Assistants The abundance of scholarly papers creates information overload for researchers. This scoping review uses the Arksey and O’Malley methodology to analyze existing AI-based technologies for literature review. It defines the functions of Google Scholar Labs, Scopus AI, Web of Science Research Assistant, NotebookLM, Elicit, Research Rabbit, Connected Papers, and LeapSpace documented in 31 recent studies from 2022 to 2026. The literature review examines literature discovery, evidence screening, citation management, and mapping, as well as uncovering research gaps and synthesizing scholarly evidence. These tools can reduce the time it takes to manage a large volume of literature and help researchers uncover relevant literature, understand contradictory or disconnected literature, and even reveal new research paths. It can help answer research questions. However, it can create risks of inaccurate information, plagiarism, bias, privacy concerns, and overreliance on automation for research synthesis. title: EFL Teachers’ Perceptions of Ethical AI Use in Teaching, Learning, and Assessment: Insights from an Omani University Context
text_snippet: EFL Teachers’ Perceptions of Ethical AI Use in Teaching, Learning, and Assessment: Insights from an Omani University Context This study investigates English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teachers’ perceptions of ethical artificial intelligence (AI) use in teaching, learning, and assessment within an Omani higher education context. Despite rapid AI adoption in education, institutional governance frameworks remain critically underdeveloped, particularly in EFL contexts — creating an urgent need for empirical, locally grounded research. Using a convergent mixed-methods design, quantitative data were collected from 52 EFL faculty members through a structured 52-item Likert-scale questionnaire, complemented by focus group discussions with nine purposively selected teachers drawn from the same participant pool. Analysis across five constructs revealed high levels of AI literacy and ethical awareness (M = 4.09), ethical responsibility and academic integrity (M = 4.19), and positive pedagogical engagement (M = 4.11). The most critical finding was a significant institutional policy deficit reflected in the lowest construct mean (M = 3.25), with the majority of participants reporting an absence of clear guidelines, consequences, or detection tools. title: Exploring Saudi Female University Students’ English Narrative Writing Experiences and Perceptions in Fictional and Nonfictional Genres
text_snippet: Exploring Saudi Female University Students’ English Narrative Writing Experiences and Perceptions in Fictional and Nonfictional Genres Despite its pedagogical value, narrative writing remains underutilized in Saudi English as a Foreign Language (EFL) curricula, and limited research has examined Saudi female university students’ experiences and perceptions of fictional and nonfiction genres. This study explored the integration of narrative writing as a genre into the English language teaching curriculum for university learners in Saudi Arabia, articulated the underlying theoretical framework, and examined the role of narratives in EFL classrooms. It combined quantitative and qualitative techniques to evaluate the experiences and perceptions of personal narrative writing and to inform the design of meaningful literacy tasks for language learners. Students’ narratives were analyzed using content and thematic approaches, supplemented by descriptive and linguistic analyses. Their responses to the task-completion questions were examined to understand their perceptions of the writing experience and emotional engagement. title: Repurposing Internship Programs for EFL Students: A Study of the Perceptions of Students and Training Institution Representatives
text_snippet: Repurposing Internship Programs for EFL Students: A Study of the Perceptions of Students and Training Institution Representatives Universities offer internship programs to help students apply academic knowledge, gain skills, and support future careers. These programs should be updated to meet evolving labor market demands. In EFL, emphasis has been on pre-service teacher education, with internships for EFL learners. Studies on internships for EFL students in non-educational courses, such as literature and translation, are few. Given the importance of English in globalization and soft skills aligned with SDG 4, addressing this gap is vital. The current study surveyed 82 EFL interns who completed 8-week training at 24 organizations, as well as their representatives. It evaluates internship programs for EFL students in non-educational tracks by examining the perceptions of interns and representatives of training institutions to improve curricula and better meet labor market needs. Quantitative data (intern responses) were analyzed descriptively and with t-tests in SPSS, while qualitative data (institution responses) were analyzed thematically using MAXQDA. title: Expert-Guided Microteaching and Teaching Performance Development in Indonesian EFL Teacher Professional Education
text_snippet: Expert-Guided Microteaching and Teaching Performance Development in Indonesian EFL Teacher Professional Education Indonesian Teacher Professional Education programs need practice-based approaches that help pre-service teachers translate pedagogical knowledge into observable classroom performance. This study examined how expert-guided microteaching was associated with teaching performance development among English as a Foreign Language pre-service teachers during university-based microteaching and how this development was reflected during school-based internships. The study provides performance-based evidence that expert guidance may help bridge the gap between simulated teaching and authentic classroom practice. A longitudinal embedded mixed-methods design with a single-group equivalent time-series repeated-measures structure was employed. Eleven English as a Foreign Language pre-service teachers participated in expert-guided microteaching and subsequently completed teaching internships in secondary schools. Quantitative data were collected through repeated classroom observations using a four-point teaching performance observation sheet and analyzed using descriptive statistics and General Linear Model repeated-measures tests. title: Enhancing Metacognitive Awareness in English Reading Through Collaborative Learning with Periodical Texts and Online Workspace
text_snippet: Enhancing Metacognitive Awareness in English Reading Through Collaborative Learning with Periodical Texts and Online Workspace The use of simplified text in English reading textbooks is crucial for teaching language features, building a sense of familiarity, and improving comprehension skills. However, exclusive dependence on such texts may encourage passive reading practices and engagement with content at a surface level, thus limiting the development of metacognitive awareness in reading. This study proposed the intervention of periodical texts within an online collaborative workspace to promote more active reading practices. Through this approach, this study examines its effects on learners’ metacognitive awareness. Adopting a mixed-methods quasi-experimental design and think-aloud protocol, the study involved foundation students at a public university in Malaysia. The experimental group demonstrated significant improvements in seven strategies namely declarative knowledge, procedural knowledge, conditional knowledge, planning, comprehension monitoring, information management, and evaluation. title: Formative Assessment Practices as Predictors of Self-Regulated Learning among University EFL Students in Vietnam
text_snippet: Formative Assessment Practices as Predictors of Self-Regulated Learning among University EFL Students in Vietnam Formative assessment can support self-regulated learning, yet limited empirical evidence has established how specific formative assessment practices predict different dimensions of self-regulated learning in Vietnamese higher education. This study examined university EFL students’ levels of self-regulated learning and perceptions of formative assessment practices, investigated the relationship between the two constructs, and determined the predictive contributions of teacher feedback, peer feedback, and self-assessment and reflection to overall self-regulated learning and its dimensions. Using a quantitative cross-sectional predictive design, data were collected through a 50-item self-report questionnaire completed by 268 undergraduate students at a public university in Vietnam. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression analyses were conducted. Students reported relatively high levels of self-regulated learning and generally positive perceptions of formative assessment. title: Adaptive AI in EFL Higher Education Instructional Contexts: Credibility and Students’ Learning Engagement
text_snippet: Adaptive AI in EFL Higher Education Instructional Contexts: Credibility and Students’ Learning Engagement As Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools collect data from both reliable and unreliable sources across the internet, concerns have been raised about the credibility of the output content learners are exposed to when seeking these tools for assistance. To address this problematic issue, our study tests the development of a pedagogical assistant trained on a personalized course framework; Besides its equipment with content that aligns with classroom lectures, the virtual assistant was given a comprehensive set of instructions guiding its behavior; Restricting its responses to the provided course material, forbidding the provision of information from any external sources as an initial action to battle against information credibility issues, and limiting its interactions to course-related discussions to promote engagement and mitigate distractions. The study explores the perceived credibility of the tested agent alongside the perceived impact on students’ learning engagement. This study is significant in informing the design of credible, curriculum-aligned AI assistants for EFL learning contexts. title: Communicative Language Teaching (CLT), Multilingual Classrooms, and NEP 2020: Evidence from Indian Higher Education
text_snippet: Communicative Language Teaching (CLT), Multilingual Classrooms, and NEP 2020: Evidence from Indian Higher Education Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) has become a dominant approach to English language education; however, empirical evidence regarding its effectiveness in multilingual Indian higher education remains limited. This study investigates the implementation of CLT in multilingual English language classrooms at Jaipur Engineering College and Research Centre (JECRC) University and the University of Engineering and Management (UEM), Jaipur, with particular emphasis on communicative competence, learner engagement, multilingual classroom practices, and alignment with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 300 undergraduate students using a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson’s correlation, and multiple regression. The findings indicate that students hold positive perceptions of CLT and that communicative teaching practices significantly enhance communicative competence and learner engagement. title: From Language Learning to Multilingual Pedagogy: A Bibliometric-Systematic Review of CLIL Research in Primary English Education
text_snippet: From Language Learning to Multilingual Pedagogy: A Bibliometric-Systematic Review of CLIL Research in Primary English Education Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) has become an important approach for simultaneously developing language proficiency and subject knowledge. Yet, research specifically addressing its application in primary English education remains dispersed across pedagogical, linguistic, and multilingual perspectives. This study aimed to map contemporary CLIL scholarship and synthesize empirical evidence concerning its pedagogical practices, learner outcomes, and implementation challenges in primary English education. A Bibliometric-Systematic Literature Review (B-SLR) was conducted using the Scopus database. Bibliographic coupling analysis was performed on 249 open-access English-language articles published between 2021 and 2025, and systematic screening, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) procedures, identified 22 empirical primary-level studies for thematic synthesis. Four intellectual clusters emerged, reflecting multilingual pedagogical innovation, language and curriculum integration, learner engagement, and teacher professional development. title: Professional Competencies of English Language Teachers in Azerbaijan: Challenges and Perspectives
text_snippet: Professional Competencies of English Language Teachers in Azerbaijan: Challenges and Perspectives The professional competence of English language teachers has become increasingly important as English continues to play a significant role in academic, professional, and socio-economic contexts. This study examines the professional competencies of English language teachers in Azerbaijan, focusing on spoken English proficiency, classroom communication, lesson planning, instructional clarity, and teachers’ confidence in supporting student learning. The study is significant because empirical research addressing thes Azerbaijani context. A mixed-methods research design was employed, and data were collected from 39 English language teachers through a structured questionnaire, self-assessment measures, and qualitative responses. The findings indicate that participants generally reported high levels of spoken English proficiency and confidence in classroom communication. However, the results also identify areas requiring further development, particularly idiomatic language use, professional communication, the clarity and alignment of learning objectives, access to specialized resources, and opportunities for targeted professional development. title: The Impact of Online Learning on the Sustainable Development of Saudi EFL Majors’ Metacognitive and Motivational Regulation: A Self-Determination-Theoretic Perspective
text_snippet: The Impact of Online Learning on the Sustainable Development of Saudi EFL Majors’ Metacognitive and Motivational Regulation: A Self-Determination-Theoretic Perspective By adopting a self-determination-theoretic perspective, this paper examines the impact of online learning on the sustainable development of Saudi English as a Foreign Language (EFL) majors’ metacognitive and motivational regulation. The study focuses on three learning constructs: metacognitive awareness, strategic autonomy, and motivational control. A mixed-methods design is employed by incorporating quantitative data from a validated self-regulated learning questionnaire into qualitative insights from semi-structured interviews with EFL instructors at a Saudi university. There are three findings of the study: First, online learning contributes significantly to students’ metacognitive awareness as a result of planning, monitoring, and reflecting on their activities. Second, online learning improves strategic autonomy through independent strategy choice and adaptation in an interactive digital environment. Third, motivational control is developed due to increased perception of autonomy, task importance, and motivation for learning. title: GenAI-Mediated English Text-Work Breadth and Localized English Acceptance in Teaching: The Role of Linguistic-Norm Awareness
text_snippet: GenAI-Mediated English Text-Work Breadth and Localized English Acceptance in Teaching: The Role of Linguistic-Norm Awareness This study investigated whether pre-service English teachers’ breadth of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-mediated English text work is associated with their awareness of linguistic norms embedded in GenAI suggestions and with their subsequent acceptance of localized English in teaching. By focusing on the micro-level mechanism linking everyday GenAI-assisted revision to pedagogical dispositions toward linguistic plurality, the study addresses a tension extending beyond China to teacher education worldwide, as GenAI-driven standardization conflicts with the value of local Englishes. Its novelty lies in testing linguistic-norm awareness as a mediator through a temporally separated design, rather than assuming exposure alone transforms attitudes. The study surveyed 316 Chinese pre-service teachers across three waves, controlling for baseline acceptance, and estimated associations via confirmatory factor analysis and a baseline-adjusted path model. Results showed that broader GenAI text work was reliably associated with linguistic-norm awareness. title: AI-Supported Self-Directed Learning and Learner Autonomy among Arab EFL Learners: A Systematic Review (2021–2026)
text_snippet: AI-Supported Self-Directed Learning and Learner Autonomy among Arab EFL Learners: A Systematic Review (2021–2026) Arab learners remain underrepresented in the international AI in education literature, and this review aims to address that gap. It examines how AI facilitates personalized and self-directed learning in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) within Arab settings. The review synthesizes empirical evidence on learner autonomy, self-regulation, and metacognitive development to identify the pedagogical, technical, cultural, and institutional factors influencing implementation in Arab classrooms. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 156 empirical articles published between 2021 and 2026 in Q1 or Q2 journals were collected, assessed for quality, and analyzed through narrative synthesis. Results show that conversational agents, intelligent tutoring systems, and adaptive platforms promote autonomy, self-regulation, and metacognitive skills, with notable improvements in writing and speaking. Nonetheless, challenges include over-dependence on AI output, uneven technological infrastructure, limited teacher training, and a disconnect between AI personalization and traditional teacher-centered approaches prevalent in many Arab educational systems. title: English for Nursing Purposes in EFL Contexts: A Systematic Review of Communication Outcomes and Curriculum Alignment
text_snippet: English for Nursing Purposes in EFL Contexts: A Systematic Review of Communication Outcomes and Curriculum Alignment The globalization of healthcare has intensified the need for effective English communication among nursing professionals, particularly for students in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) and English as a Second Language (ESL) contexts. As English increasingly functions as a lingua franca in healthcare, nursing education must address the limitations of general English instruction in preparing students for the communicative demands of clinical practice. This systematic review examines the effectiveness of English for Specific Purposes (ESP) programs in enhancing nursing students’ clinical communication skills across diverse educational and cultural contexts. By synthesizing fragmented evidence across educational settings, this review provides an evidence-based foundation for curriculum development, pedagogical practice, and future research in nursing English education. Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, a comprehensive search was conducted across ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, CINAHL, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and 2025. title: A Comparative Analysis of Linguistic Features in EFL Narrative Writing: English Program and Thai Program Students in Thailand
text_snippet: A Comparative Analysis of Linguistic Features in EFL Narrative Writing: English Program and Thai Program Students in Thailand This study examines similarities and differences in linguistic features and determines the linguistic features most commonly used in English narrative writing by Grade 6 students enrolled in an English Program and those in a Thai Program at a demonstration school in Bangkok. This comparative quantitative descriptive study provides insights into how different learning programs may relate to students’ linguistic performance in writing, and it helps identify the areas for improvement in linguistics and writing. Various studies have examined the English writing of Thai EFL students; however, research on a comparative analysis of linguistic features in EFL narrative writing remains limited. Three linguistic features are highlighted: lexical, syntactic, and discourse. Forty-nine participants, selected through convenience sampling, produced five narrative texts of about 100 words each. Data were gathered using a narrative worksheet for writing samples; AntConc to tabulate lexical density and diversity; and Coh-Metrix to calculate syntactic complexity, coherence, and lexical cohesion. title: Willingness to Communicate in English Language Learning in Higher Education: A Bibliometric-Systematic Review of Research Trends, Influencing Factors, and Future Directions
text_snippet: Willingness to Communicate in English Language Learning in Higher Education: A Bibliometric-Systematic Review of Research Trends, Influencing Factors, and Future Directions Willingness to Communicate is an important dimension of English language learning because it reflects learners’ readiness to use English when communication opportunities arise. As higher education increasingly emphasizes communicative competence, understanding the factors that facilitate or constrain students’ willingness to communicate has become particularly important. This study examines the intellectual structure, research trends, and thematic developments of willingness to communicate in English-language learning among higher-education students. By integrating large-scale knowledge mapping with an in-depth synthesis of empirical evidence, the study provides a more comprehensive understanding of how willingness to communicate has developed and the factors shaping students’ communication engagement. A two-stage Bibliometric-Systematic Literature Review was conducted. The bibliometric stage analyzed 193 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2021 and 2025 using bibliographic coupling and VOSviewer, followed by a systematic review of 25 empirical studies selected through Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-guided screening process. title: Unfocused Corrective Feedback and L2 Writing CAF: The Moderating Role of Individual Differences
text_snippet: Unfocused Corrective Feedback and L2 Writing CAF: The Moderating Role of Individual Differences Research on written corrective feedback in second language learning has advanced, addressing uncertainties about its effectiveness. The debate now centres on the most effective way to give feedback. However, controversy persists, and research on unfocused feedback remains scarce. This quasi-experimental study examines the effects of unfocused written corrective feedback—direct, indirect, and metalinguistic—on the complexity, accuracy, and fluency of 139 English-as-a-second-language learners’ writing at an English-medium instruction university in the United Arab Emirates. It also investigates the moderating effects of individual-difference variables—language aptitude, attitudes towards written corrective feedback, and second-language proficiency—on feedback efficacy. Three experimental groups and one control group wrote essays (pre-test), revised their drafts (post-test), and composed essays on new topics (delayed post-test) over fourteen weeks. MANCOVA results revealed that participants who received direct and metalinguistic feedback showed reduced fluency compared with those in the indirect feedback and control groups. title: The Use of Automated Written Corrective Feedback Tools by Learners of English as a Foreign Language at Saudi Tertiary Education
text_snippet: The Use of Automated Written Corrective Feedback Tools by Learners of English as a Foreign Language at Saudi Tertiary Education This study explored the effectiveness of automated written corrective feedback (AWCF) in learning English as a foreign language among undergraduate students in Saudi tertiary education, focusing on how learners responded to and benefited from it. Using a mixed-methods approach, data were collected from students’ written drafts before and after using AWCF and from a structured questionnaire capturing their perceptions and engagement. The findings showed that AWCF helped students identify and revise grammatical and spelling errors, improving surface-level linguistic accuracy. Students also demonstrated high engagement, critically assessing feedback, particularly for local proper nouns and context-specific language use. Although students largely trusted AWCF, they did not accept all suggestions, demonstrating self-monitoring and writing autonomy. The findings underscore the importance of teacher involvement in addressing higher-order concerns. The study recommends integrating AWCF with teacher feedback to maximize learning outcomes. title: The Effect of Teacher Support on Saudi EFL Learners’ Writing Quality: A Quasi-Experimental Study
text_snippet: The Effect of Teacher Support on Saudi EFL Learners’ Writing Quality: A Quasi-Experimental Study This study investigates the effect of structured multidimensional teacher support on the writing quality of Saudi English as a foreign language learners and explores how they perceive the support provided during L2 writing instruction. The study provides empirical evidence on the role of structured multidimensional teacher support in improving EFL learners’ writing quality, a topic that has received limited attention in intervention-based research. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was employed with 81 Saudi female undergraduate students enrolled in an academic writing course. Students in the experimental group received structured multidimensional teacher support, whereas those in the control group followed regular writing instruction. Writing quality was assessed using an analytic writing rubric, and learners’ perceptions were measured through a questionnaire. The findings revealed significant improvements in the experimental group’s overall writing quality as well as in content, organization, vocabulary, and language use. title: Genre-Based Variation in AI-Assisted Students’ English-Indonesian Translation Quality: A Comparative Assessment across Academic Texts, News Texts, and Poetry
text_snippet: Genre-Based Variation in AI-Assisted Students’ English-Indonesian Translation Quality: A Comparative Assessment across Academic Texts, News Texts, and Poetry Artificial Intelligence (AI) performance in translation varies across genres due to the unique features of each genre. This study aims to explore the quality of students’ AI-aided translations of English academic texts, news articles, and poetry, and to determine whether translation quality varies by genre. A descriptive comparative research design was used in the study, involving a sample of 35 students from the English Departments of four universities in Indonesia. The participants translated an English academic text, a news article, and a poem using an Artificial Intelligence-assisted translation tool. The total number of translations was 105. Six translation experts evaluated all the translation samples using Nababan and Nuraeni’s model. They assessed translation quality in terms of accuracy, acceptability, readability, and a new dimension proposed by the researchers, i.e., poeticness, specifically for the translation of poetry. The study found that translations produced by students using AI ranged from moderate to high in quality. title: Integrating a Global Language Framework into Tertiary Curriculum Reform: Responses of English Language Teachers in Vietnam
text_snippet: Integrating a Global Language Framework into Tertiary Curriculum Reform: Responses of English Language Teachers in Vietnam As part of the extended National Foreign Languages Project (2008–2035), Vietnam has adopted the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) as a top-down strategy to enhance the quality of English teaching and learning. This study examines how English teachers responded to this curriculum reform at a Vietnamese university. Using a mixed-methods sequential design, the study collected data through questionnaires with 36 EFL teachers and in-depth interviews with 8. The findings reveal that while teachers are making various efforts to adapt to the CEFR-aligned curriculum, most changes remain limited to coping techniques. Instead of helping students attain the required level of language proficiency, teachers primarily adopt strategies designed to help students pass the compulsory CEFR-aligned exams, viewing this as a necessary teaching adjustment. At the grassroots level, the teachers who have not yet gained ownership of the change and who lack institutional support continue to rely primarily on short-term, situational strategies rather than sustainable approaches to improving students’ overall language proficiency. title: The Effects of Theme-Based Narrow Reading on Business English Vocabulary Acquisition among Chinese EFL College Students
text_snippet: The Effects of Theme-Based Narrow Reading on Business English Vocabulary Acquisition among Chinese EFL College Students Vocabulary plays a significant role in language learning and language development. It is important to acquire sufficient vocabulary to ensure effective communication. Some studies show the efficiency of narrow reading for general and academic vocabulary learning, but fewer studies investigate the effects of narrow reading on technical vocabulary, such as Business English vocabulary. This study aimed to investigate Business English vocabulary acquisition through theme-based narrow reading. The main purpose of this study was to fill the literature gap on learning Business English vocabulary through narrow reading, thereby contributing to the broader field of second language acquisition. This study employed a one-group quasi-experimental design and utilized purposive sampling to recruit twenty-five Chinese first-year students majoring in Business English, together with one Business English teacher as an instructor. This study covered quantitative and qualitative data, but this article only focuses on the quantitative part. title: AI-Powered Automated Speaking Scoring and Human Evaluation: A Comparative Study of EFL Learners’ Oral Proficiency
text_snippet: AI-Powered Automated Speaking Scoring and Human Evaluation: A Comparative Study of EFL Learners’ Oral Proficiency Recent advances in artificial intelligence have led to the development of automated speaking assessment systems capable of evaluating oral proficiency with increasing accuracy. This study compares Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered automated speaking scoring and human evaluation in assessing the oral proficiency of 74 Saudi English as Foreign Language (EFL) learners. Participants completed a picture-description speaking task, which was evaluated by both Claude and two trained human raters using identical holistic and analytic speaking rubrics. The study examined holistic speaking scores and five analytic dimensions: coherence, cohesion, content development, grammar, and vocabulary. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, comparative analyses, Intraclass Correlation Coefficients (ICC), Weighted Kappa coefficients, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results showed no significant difference between AI-generated and human-assigned holistic speaking scores. title: Artificial Intelligence in Supporting Self-Regulated Reading among English as a Second Language Learners: A Systematic Review
text_snippet: Artificial Intelligence in Supporting Self-Regulated Reading among English as a Second Language Learners: A Systematic Review Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly prominent in English language education, offering new possibilities for supporting reading instruction and independent learning among English as a second language (ESL) learner. This study aims to examine the existing body of empirical research concerning the use of AI to improve reading skills and encourage self-regulated learning (SRL). The significance of this study lies in its synthesis of fragmented data to provide a unified framework for future technology-mediated reading instruction. Using a systematic literature review approach that strictly followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, 19 empirical studies were extracted from major academic databases including Scopus, ERIC, and Google Scholar and analyzed through thematic analysis. The synthesized results reveal that AI applications, particularly adaptive learning platforms and conversational agents, effectively support reading development by giving feedback, personal learning experiences, and opportunities for learners to monitor their own progress. title: Mixed Learning Environment for Learning English as a Foreign Language: The Post-COVID Kazakh Context in the Central Asia
text_snippet: Mixed Learning Environment for Learning English as a Foreign Language: The Post-COVID Kazakh Context in the Central Asia The COVID-19 pandemic considerably reshaped higher education, prompting universities worldwide to expand their reliance on online and blended modes of teaching and learning. This study investigates students’ experiences, preferences, and perceived effectiveness of mixed learning environments in the post-pandemic context of Kazakhstan. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, involving 515 undergraduate students from three universities in Astana. Data was collected through a structured online questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson’s Chi-square tests. The findings indicate that while 42.5% of students prefer traditional face-to-face instruction due to higher motivation and interaction, a majority (50.7%) favor blended learning as it combines flexibility with instructional effectiveness. Only six to seven% of respondents support online learning. Furthermore, 74.8% of students expressed a preference for retaining online elements particularly recorded lectures within future teaching models. title: Curriculum-Embedded Song-Based English Language Instruction: Effects on Vocabulary Acquisition and Humanistic Value Internalization in Early Childhood Education
text_snippet: Curriculum-Embedded Song-Based English Language Instruction: Effects on Vocabulary Acquisition and Humanistic Value Internalization in Early Childhood Education English programs in early childhood education now focus heavily on cognitive and linguistic benchmarks, but three issues tend to get overlooked in the process: affective and moral development are usually theorized on their own, language outcomes and prosocial outcomes are studied separately, and songs are still treated as a bonus activity rather than a genuine part of the curriculum. This study set out to address those gaps by developing a 12-week, curriculum-embedded song-based English program designed to build vocabulary and instill humanistic values in children aged four to six simultaneously. Using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design, 60 children were divided into an intervention group (n = 30) and a control group (n = 30). title: Enhancing English Pronunciation through YouTube Videos in a Blended Learning Environment: An Experimental Mixed-Methods Study
text_snippet: Enhancing English Pronunciation through YouTube Videos in a Blended Learning Environment: An Experimental Mixed-Methods Study This study is an attempt towards exploring pedagogic significance of YouTube videos related to learning of pronunciation in English as foreign language context. The scope of the study emphasizes the effect of YouTube-integrated instruction on accelerating English pronunciation skills within a blended learning landscape in Uzbekistan. Employing a quasi-experimental, mixed-methods design with both quantitative and qualitative data collection to study the cause-and-effect, the research involved a sample of 40 graduation students which was selected by purposive sampling, and assigned to control (n = 20) and experimental (n = 20) groups. The experimental group was given twelve weeks of pronunciation training using curated YouTube videos, while the control group was taught by the routine traditional method. A pronunciation assessment tool was developed and was later validated by five TESOL/ELT experts (CVI = 0.92), was administered as pre- and post-intervention. Reliability was confirmed through a pilot study (Cronbach’s α = 0.88). title: Finding a Voice: Lexical Bundles in Literary Writing in the Omani EFL Context
text_snippet: Finding a Voice: Lexical Bundles in Literary Writing in the Omani EFL Context Authorial voice is an integral component of literary writing where interpretation and analysis play an important role. Based on Hyland (2008), this study focuses on functional lexical bundles, including text, participant, and referential-oriented bundles, to analyze samples of undergraduate students’ writings in literature in an L1 Arabic EFL context. This article aims to investigate the extent to which students’ written essays in literature used lexical bundles as a linguistic resource to assert their individual voice and stylistic identity. The study is significant as it contributes to an understanding of how lexical bundle usage shapes authorial voice among undergraduates, particularly in an L1 Arabic EFL context. The present corpus comprises 157 undergraduate literary essays from a public university in Oman. The corpus is over 90, 000 words. Analysis of frequency, variation, and functional roles is done using Ant Conc 4.0 software. title: Artificial Intelligence as a Pedagogical Bridge in Education Reform: Localizing EFL Listening Materials through Generative AI in Resource-Constrained Contexts
text_snippet: Artificial Intelligence as a Pedagogical Bridge in Education Reform: Localizing EFL Listening Materials through Generative AI in Resource-Constrained Contexts Listening instruction in many English as a Foreign Language (EFL) contexts continues to rely on globally produced audio materials that are linguistically accurate but culturally distant from learners’ lived experiences. Contextualized pedagogy is widely advocated, yet teachers often lack the resources to produce high-quality localized audio. This study investigates how generative artificial intelligence (AI) supports the development of contextualized listening materials and influences students’ listening experiences. A qualitative multi-site case study was conducted in eight secondary schools across geographically diverse areas of West Kalimantan, Indonesia. English teachers and 32 students participated in the design and classroom implementation of AI-supported listening materials. Data were collected through pre- and post-development teacher interviews, classroom reflections, and post-implementation student interviews. The data were analyzed thematically and compared across cases. The findings show that generative AI functioned not merely as a productivity tool but as a form of pedagogical infrastructure. title: Simulated Empathy and Human Response: A Comparative Analysis of AI and Human Emotional Interaction
text_snippet: Simulated Empathy and Human Response: A Comparative Analysis of AI and Human Emotional Interaction This qualitative comparative study examines how ChatGPT-4o simulates empathy when responding to emotionally charged English in an EFL context. It aims to compare artificial intelligence and human responses in emotional recognition, pragmatic tone, empathetic support, and linguistic authenticity. The study is significant because EFL interaction requires learners to interpret affective cues while selecting socially and culturally appropriate language. Fifty prompts generated 50 AI responses and 1,000 human responses from 20 advanced-level EFL learners; the data were organized into 50 prompt-level comparison sets and analyzed through qualitative content analysis and comparative discourse analysis. Two trained coders applied a hybrid framework and achieved substantial agreement (Cohen’s κ = .86). ChatGPT recognized the intended emotion in 88% of its responses, used an appropriate tone in 84%, and displayed empathetic and pragmatically relevant support in 90%. title: Omani Ways of Criticizing in WhatsApp Discourse: A Pragmatic Analysis
text_snippet: Omani Ways of Criticizing in WhatsApp Discourse: A Pragmatic Analysis In a globalized and globalizing world, intercultural communication is a necessity for various reasons, such as commerce, education, politics, and tourism, calling for ethnographic studies with special focus on the pragmatics of different speech acts. Pragmatics of speech act can be different from culture to culture: not knowing these differences can lead to misunderstandings or even disagreements. This problem exacerbates in the virtual setting, where interlocutors lack the same nonverbal indications and cues that would otherwise support the expression of meaning and intention. This study probes into the ways in which Omani interlocutors perform and interpret the speech act of criticism in asynchronous WhatsApp interactions. Adopting the six-phase thematic analysis framework of Braun and Clarke (2006), the study qualitatively analyzes 13 WhatsApp interactions with different categorial criticisms (see Pyne et al., 2024). Findings reveal that Omani ways of criticism are influenced by Omani cultural values and that the strategies adopted for criticism differ from one context to another. title: A Comparative Pragmatic Analysis of AI-Generated and Human Apologies in Iraqi EFL Learners
text_snippet: A Comparative Pragmatic Analysis of AI-Generated and Human Apologies in Iraqi EFL Learners The present study examines the use of apology strategies in the responses of artificial intelligence and Iraqi learners of English as a foreign language. The primary research question is whether artificial intelligence is pragmatically competent like language users in producing apology responses. The study aims to compare and contrast similarities and differences in the use and distribution of apology strategies according to Cohen and Olshtain (1981) and politeness theory by Brown and Levinson (1987). This study is significant in assessing the feasibility of artificial intelligence as a framework for developing pragmatic competence and its application to cross-cultural communication. This study employs a comparative approach using a discourse completion task comprising fourteen situations that prompt apologies. Seven hundred responses were generated by artificial intelligence, and seven hundred responses by Iraqi EFL learners of English. The responses are analyzed in terms of primary apology strategies such as explicit apology, acceptance of responsibility, explanation, offer of repair, and promise of forbearance, and politeness strategies associated with power and social distance.

title: Syntactic Complexity in AI-Generated vs. Human-Authored Linguistic and Literary Texts
text_snippet: Syntactic Complexity in AI-Generated vs. Human-Authored Linguistic and Literary Texts This paper examines how the syntactic complexity of academic writing is affected mainly by the source of authorship (AI-generated or human) or by the genre of disciplinary writing (linguistic or literary). The primary purpose is to test the syntactic-complexity differences between these variables and to establish the degree of influence of genre conventions on structural variation. The importance of the research is that it adds to the existing discussions about AI as a phenomenon in academic writing and, specifically, whether AI-generated texts are capable of syntactically reproducing the specific norms of a specific discipline of writing. To this end, the comparative corpus-based design was used. The sample consisted of 20 introduction sections: equal numbers of linguistic and literary texts and equal numbers of human-authored AI-generated texts. The Second Language Syntactic Complexity Analyzer (L2SCA) extracts fourteen syntactic complexity measures, which include length of production unit, subordination, coordination and phrasal sophistication. title: Evaluating the Automated Scoring and Feedback provided by the Virtual Writing Tutor on
text_snippet: Evaluating the Automated Scoring and Feedback provided by the Virtual Writing Tutor on This study explores the nature of automated scoring and feedback provided by an artificial intelligence-powered tool, the Virtual Writing Tutor. It also assessed the quality of the feedback specifically for non-native writers of IELTS Writing Task 1 essays. The study therefore contributes to the general research literature devoted to evaluating writing aids, which as yet has paid scant attention to this particular tool, and relatively little to the actual quality of feedback on writing for specific tasks. Eight students participated in this convergent mixed-method study, conducted during a 30-hour IELTS preparation program. A quantitative student-based perspective came from a 15 item, 5-point Likert scale response, questionnaire administered to students concerning their subjective evaluation of the Tutor’s feedback. A qualitative expert perspective came from researcher review of the automated scoring and feedback provided on the participants’ IELTS Writing Task 1 practice essays. title: Human vs AI-Generated Texts in Language Learning: A Linguistic Comparison
text_snippet: Human vs AI-Generated Texts in Language Learning: A Linguistic Comparison The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education has significantly changed how we approach language learning and teaching. Even though AI-generated materials are becoming more common in English language instruction, there is still not enough linguistic research comparing these texts with those designed for textbooks. This study aims to fill that gap by comparing human-authored and AI-generated texts used in language learning. The goal is to identify the main linguistic differences between these two types of texts and assess their effectiveness as language-learning models. The study uses texts from High Note and Language Leader alongside those generated by ChatGPT on similar topics, all within the B1–B2 proficiency range. The analysis examines lexical richness, syntactic complexity, cohesion, and discourse organization using both quantitative and qualitative methods. title: The Impact of AI-Assisted Learning in Process Writing on Learners’ Well-being
text_snippet: The Impact of AI-Assisted Learning in Process Writing on Learners’ Well-being The paper discussed the effects of using AI-assisted learning in a Process Writing Approach on writing performance and psychological well-being of EFL students. The value of the work is that the paper will examine the lack of consideration of both cognitive and emotional products in AI-assisted-writing studies. The quasi-experimental design used is a pre-test/post-test over 6 weeks, with a sample of 60 level A2 EFL students. Data were collected using the Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-being Scale, a well-being scale based on the PERMA framework, a Writing Anxiety Scale, and a test of writing skills. title: Exploring Saudi EFL Learners’ Perceptions of ChatGPT for Vocabulary Learning: A TAM-Based Descriptive Study
text_snippet: Exploring Saudi EFL Learners’ Perceptions of ChatGPT for Vocabulary Learning: A TAM-Based Descriptive Study This study investigated Saudi foreign language learners’ (EFL) perceptions of using ChatGPT for vocabulary learning through the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to answer the question: What are Saudi EFL learners’ perceptions of using ChatGPT as a vocabulary learning tool? It aimed to explore their perceptions according to perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU). Vocabulary serves as the critical initial step in learning a second language and facilitating the mastery of language skills. It allows language speakers to communicate effectively. Thus, integrating an effective artificial intelligence (AI) tool in language learning contexts is crucial. Consequently, it is important to discover whether participants believe that using ChatGPT is easy and beneficial as a vocabulary learning resource.
